food.name: Cranberries

identity.basisReason: Raw per-100g whole-fruit basis matches the FoodRanked fruit comparison lane.

scoreReadiness.summary: New FoodRanked fruit entry with USDA per-100g nutrition, explicit provenance, completed context pros/cons, approved narration override, and app-ready sprite path.
caveats: Fresh cranberry glycemic index is a context value rather than a USDA nutrient.
Real foods vary by cultivar, season, and preparation; this record is a canonical comparison entry.

sourceNotes: USDA FoodData Central 171722, Cranberries, raw, per 100g.
Daily value percentages are derived from USDA nutrients using FDA adult DVs and rounded to the nearest whole percent.
Glycemic index is a non-USDA context value for fresh cranberries and is used only as a scoring/display context signal.

topPros.title: sharp tart flavour tool
topPros.explanation: A small amount can brighten sauces, oats, salads, or baking without needing much fruit volume.

topPros.title: freezes well
topPros.explanation: It holds up well from frozen, so it is easier to keep around than many soft fresh fruits.

topPros.title: polyphenol-rich skin
topPros.explanation: The deep red skin brings a stronger plant-compound angle than many mild fruits.

topCons.title: too tart for plain snacking
topCons.explanation: Most people do not eat raw cranberries by the handful, so the practical snack role is limited.

topCons.title: products can change the deal
topCons.explanation: Cranberry sauces, juices, and dried versions often behave like a different food from plain raw berries.

topCons.title: seasonal and recipe-dependent
topCons.explanation: Fresh cranberries are not as effortless year-round as everyday fruits like apples, bananas, or berries.

explanation.summary: Carbs are carrying this food most, while minerals are holding it back most. It lands in D tier.
explanation.whyThisTier: This food lands in D tier with a display score of 20. Section scores: fats 55, carbs 70.7, proteins 0, vitamins 8, minerals 0, pros 50, cons 50.
